arxiv-2103-11969.title: Nonlinear electric conductivity and THz-induced charge transport in graphene
arxiv-2103-11969.creator: Shunsuke A. Sato, Angel Rubio
arxiv-2103-11969.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shunsuke A. Sato, Angel Rubio. Based on the quantum master equation approach, the nonlinear electric conductivity of graphene is investigated under static electric fields for various chemical potential shifts. The simulation results show that, as the field strength increases, the effective conductivity is firstly suppressed, reflecting the depletion of effective carriers due to the large displacement in the Brillouin zone caused by the strong field.

arxiv-2111-08290.title: On the inverse gamma subordinator
arxiv-2111-08290.creator: Fausto Colantoni, Mirko D’Ovidio
arxiv-2111-08290.description: Abstract In this paper we deal with some open problems concerned with gamma subordinators. In particular, we provide a representation for the moments of the inverse gamma subordinator. Then, we focus on λ \lambda -potentials and we study the governing equations associated with gamma subordinators and inverse processes.

arxiv-2210-06005.title: Generative Adversarial Nets: Can we generate a new dataset based on only one training set?
arxiv-2210-06005.creator: Lan V. Truong
arxiv-2210-06005.description: Abstract A generative adversarial network (GAN) is a class of machine learning frameworks designed by Goodfellow et al. in 2014. In the GAN framework, the generative model is pitted against an adversary: a discriminative model that learns to determine whether a sample is from the model distribution or the data distribution.

arxiv-2502-14202.title: Do LLMs Consider Security? An Empirical Study on Responses to Programming Questions
arxiv-2502-14202.creator: Amirali Sajadi (corresponding author), Binh Le, Anh Nguyen, Kostadin Damevski, Preetha Chatterjee
arxiv-2502-14202.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Amirali Sajadi (corresponding author), Binh Le, Anh Nguyen, Kostadin Damevski, Preetha Chatterjee. The widespread adoption of conversational LLMs for software development has raised new security concerns regarding the safety of LLM-generated content. Our motivational study outlines ChatGPT’s potential in volunteering context-specific information to the developers, promoting safe coding practices. Motivated by this finding, we conduct a study to evaluate the degree of security awareness exhibited by three prominent LLMs: Claude 3, GPT-4, and Llama 3.

arxiv-2506-07981.title: Real-time Localization of a Soccer Ball from a Single Camera
arxiv-2506-07981.creator: Dmitrii Vorobev, Artem Prosvetov, Karim Elhadji Daou
arxiv-2506-07981.description: Abstract We propose a computationally efficient method for real-time three-dimensional football trajectory reconstruction from a single broadcast camera. In contrast to previous work, our approach introduces a multi-mode state model with W W discrete modes to significantly accelerate optimization while preserving centimeter-level accuracy – even in cases of severe occlusion, motion blur, and complex backgrounds.

Large language models (LLMs) have been widely integrated into critical automated workflows, including contract review and job application processes. However, LLMs are susceptible to manipulation by fraudulent information, which can lead to harmful outcomes. Although advanced defense methods have been developed to address this issue, they often exhibit limitations in effectiveness, interpretability, and generalizability, particularly when applied to LLM-based applications.

pmc-11681604.title: miRNA‐6236 Regulation of Postischemic Skeletal Muscle Angiogenesis
pmc-11681604.creator: Arul M. Mani, Victor Lamin, Ronan C. Peach, Eli H. Friesen, Thomas Wong, Madhu V. Singh, Ayotunde O. Dokun
pmc-11681604.description: BackgroundPeripheral arterial disease affects >200 million people worldwide and is characterized by impaired blood flow to the lower extremities. There are no effective medical treatments available. Using the mouse hind‐limb ischemia model and miRNA sequencing, we identified a novel miRNA, miR‐6236, whose expression significantly elevated in ischemic mouse limbs compared with nonischemic limbs.

pmc-12452472.title: Atypical behavior of recurrent glioblastoma tumor cells with a highly adherent radial glial phenotype
pmc-12452472.creator: Manjusha Vaidya, Jonhoi Smith, Julia Pessaia, Melvin Field, Kiminobu Sugaya
pmc-12452472.description: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most common malignant primary brain tumor, characterized by a high recurrence rate despite aggressive therapy. We present a case of a 32-year-old male with a recurrent WHO Grade IV IDH1-mutant astrocytoma after undergoing standard Stupp protocol chemoradiation and tumor-treating field therapy.

pmc-12455086.title: A standardized metric to define a successful transition from pediatric to adult care in sickle cell disease
pmc-12455086.creator: Galia Pollock, Susanna Curtis
pmc-12455086.description: rove transfer of care practice in this vulnerable period. Today, 95% of children with SCD in the developed world will survive to adulthood. pmc-12561147.title: The Impact of Agreeableness Trait on Volunteer Service Motivation and Behavior: A Moderated Mediation Study of Chinese College Students
pmc-12561147.creator: Chen Chen, Weilin Su
pmc-12561147.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). How to continuously motivate college students to participate in voluntary activities has always been one of the burning issues in the field of educational psychology research. Based on the activation theory, this study constructed and tested a moderated mediation model to explore how to improve college students’ volunteer service motivation and behavior from the perspective of agreeableness traits and examined the moderating role of social support.

pmc-12569033.title: Structure and activation of the Drosophila insulin receptor by three Drosophila insulin-like peptides
pmc-12569033.creator: Kai Cai, Michelle Ng, Rochele R. Yamamoto, Mohammed Akhter Hossain, Catherine Hall, John D. Wade, Marc Tatar, Eunhee Choi, Xiao-chen Bai
pmc-12569033.description: Insulin/IGF signaling (IIS) is a highly conserved pathway essential for physiological regulation from yeast to mammals. In Drosophila melanogaster, a single insulin-like receptor (dmIR) interacts with various insulin-like peptides (DILPs), leading to diverse signaling and functional outcomes. However, the mechanisms by which different DILPs result in varied receptor activation and biological responses remain unclear.

pmc-12608846.title: Manipulation with Mutational Status of VHL Regulates Hypoxic Metabolism and Pro-Angiogenic Phenotypes in ccRCC Caki-1 Cells
pmc-12608846.creator: Pavel Abramov, Alexandr Mazur, Aleksey Starshin, Svetlana Zhenilo, Egor Prokhortchouk
pmc-12608846.description: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), accounting for 80–90% of renal malignancies, is frequently driven by VHL inactivation—either through mutation or promoter hypermethylation—resulting in constitutive HIF2α activation and pseudohypoxic signaling. VHL gene inactivation is a hallmark of von Hippel–Lindau syndrome, a hereditary disorder predisposing patients to ccRCC and other tumors, underscoring its central role in disease pathogenesis.

pmc-12872849.title: The Jaga Diri digital intervention improved knowledge and adherence to weekly iron-folic acid supplementation among adolescent girls in Maluku Province, Indonesia
pmc-12872849.creator: Lershito Antonio Pasamba, Christiana Rialine Titaley, Sean Samuel Istia, Ritha Tahitu, Elpira Asmin, Farah Christina Noya, Mega Clarita Laurence, Yudhie Djuhastidar Tando, Maxwell Landri Vers Malakauseya, Liyani Sartika Sara
pmc-12872849.description: IntroductionAdherence to weekly iron/folic acid (IFA) supplementation, a vital intervention to combat anaemia among adolescent girls, remains a global challenge, including in Maluku Province, Indonesia. This study assessed the effect of “Jaga Diri” application, in enhancing knowledge and adherence to IFA supplementation among adolescent girls from Salahutu Sub-District of Maluku Province, Indonesia.

pmc-13093474.title: Studies of Water Films and Carbonation via Neutron Scattering and Infrared Adsorption: In Situ Studies of Mg(OH)2 and Ca(OH)2
pmc-13093474.creator: Hubert King, Ryan Murphy, Avery Baumann, Robert Dalgliesh, Dirk Honecker, Greg Smith
pmc-13093474.description: Small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) and polarization-modulation infrared reflection–absorption spectroscopy (PM-IRRAS) were used to investigate the coupled evolution of nanometer water films and carbonation products in Ca­(OH)2 and Mg­(OH)2 under humidified CO2. Quantitative SANS modeling demonstrates that subnanometer adsorbed films on Ca­(OH)2 and thicker (≈1–2 nm) D2O films on Mg­(OH)2 mediate ion transport and isotopic exchange at buried interfaces.
